articles.title: Home Assistant revises HTTPS advice to keep older devices connected
articles.dek: The revised default preserves access for Voice Preview Edition, Sonos and older Android clients.
body: Home Assistant changes its recommended HTTPS encryption profile to Intermediate v6, keeping connections from devices that cannot use TLS 1.3. These include current Home Assistant Voice Preview Edition firmware, the companion app on Android 6–9 and Sonos speakers fetching speech or music. New installations use the same revised default.

This reverses the Modern v6 recommendation covered earlier this month. Intermediate v6 still removes older encryption methods while accepting TLS 1.2; Modern v6 remains an option when every connecting device supports TLS 1.3.

The repair also explains that the certificate itself does not need replacing. Its five-minute recovery trial checks browser access, so owners still need to check their devices and apps after confirming. These settings affect incoming HTTPS connections, not Home Assistant’s outgoing connections.

pullRequests.title: Recommend Intermediate v6 and clarify the http SSL profile repair
Recommend the Intermediate v6 SSL profile in the HTTP docs

articles.title: Music Assistant charts what you listen to
articles.dek: A new Statistics page brings favourite artists, listening patterns and play counts together.
body: Music Assistant adds a Statistics page showing which music fills a listener’s days. A period picker moves from today to the past week, month, year or all recorded history, with play counts, favourite artists, genres and a chart of listening over time.

A summary on Discover links to the full page, where a weekday-and-hour map shows listening patterns alongside the most-played tracks, albums, artists and playlists. Artists with the same name stay separate, and the display refreshes after a completed track.

The figures use completed-play records. Listening time is an estimate from those events; the earlier history change started a new record rather than reconstructing older listening from saved resume positions.

articles.title: Supervisor’s stable update includes an app-repository security correction
articles.dek: Version 2026.10.5 also repairs network settings and storage failures on affected installations.
body: Home Assistant Supervisor 2026.10.5 reaches the stable channel with a security correction involving app repositories. Stefan Agner’s release announcement identifies it as the update’s most notable change.

The update also makes a configured smaller network packet size take effect for containers, restores Wi-Fi scans around network names with unsupported text encoding, and lets data-disk moves use NVMe drives that incorrectly report zero capacity.

articles.title: ESPHome shows when Mitsubishi heat pumps actually heat or cool
articles.dek: Operating history and horizontal airflow controls give owners a clearer view of a mini-split’s work.
body: ESPHome reads whether a compatible Mitsubishi mini-split is actively heating or cooling, rather than showing only its selected mode. Home Assistant can display that activity and keep it in the climate history. The status normally updates with the temperature readings, once a minute by default.
Companion controls let owners aim the horizontal vane to either side, split the airflow or make it swing. Automations can read and set both horizontal and vertical vane directions together.

Units that do not supply the operating-status response keep working, but cannot report measured heating or cooling activity. Kyle Boone makes his first ESPHome contribution with the activity reporting; Boris Krivonog supplies the airflow controls.

articles.title: Home Assistant explores forecast answers alongside future sensor charts
articles.dek: The revised proposal puts AI access, Nord Pool prices and solar forecasts in its first scope; visual automation controls may follow later.
body: Home Assistant is shaping a forecast system that would let AI conversation agents answer questions about future sensor values, alongside charts extending beyond the present. The revised proposal includes Nord Pool day-ahead electricity prices and existing solar-forecast integrations in its minimum scope.

A sensor’s more-info chart, the History panel and history graph cards would show future values distinctly from measurements and identify their source. Visual triggers for predicted thresholds or cheaper periods remain in the proposal, but can be dropped from the first delivery if time runs out. The underlying design still needs agreement.

Markus Tuominen has argued for starting with one forecast per sensor while leaving room for later extensions. That limit remains: resident-added forecasts, multiple sources and uncertainty bands are follow-up work.

articles.title: ESPHome calibrates presence radar for the room around it
articles.dek: LD2410 modules gain a calibration button and an explicit result without HiLink’s PC tool.
body: ESPHome exposes the LD2410 radar’s built-in background-noise calibration, allowing makers to set its detection thresholds for a room without using HiLink’s PC tool. The routine needs module firmware 2.44 or newer and an empty detection area, with fans and ventilation running as usual.

A button starts a measurement lasting 10 to 120 seconds. Optional sensors show when it is running and whether the module reports success or failure; a completed run without either result is marked Unconfirmed. ESPHome then reads back the thresholds the radar chose.

bhuveshm29 makes their first ESPHome contribution with the addition, continuing an earlier proposal by anunayk. The contributor reports hardware use of the same calibration logic on LD2410C modules; this port and its refusal handling were checked by compilation.

pullRequests.title: [ld2410] Add automatic background noise correction

articles.title: Powersensor brings local energy readings into Home Assistant
articles.dek: Automatically discovered plugs send their updates over the home network without a cloud dependency.
body: Australian households using Powersensor energy monitors gain a local connection to Home Assistant. The new integration discovers its plugs automatically and receives pushed readings across the home network, without depending on the manufacturer’s cloud.
The connection is bookman-dius’s first contribution to Home Assistant Core.

pullRequests.title: Add Powersensor integration

articles.title: Z-Wave JS keeps secure pairing tied to the chosen device
articles.dek: Messages from another node cannot satisfy the exchange that establishes its security keys.
body: Z-Wave JS checks that messages establishing an S2 secure connection come from the device being paired. Another node can no longer satisfy those waiting steps by supplying key-exchange or completion commands.
The driver also rejects invalid public keys, retrieves only the keys both requested and granted, and verifies that the final completion message uses the temporary pairing key.

pullRequests.title: fix: harden S2 message parsing and bootstrapping

articles.title: Home Assistant explains how to take part in November’s feedback month
articles.dek: Search first, describe one problem per topic and invite the rest of the household to contribute.
body: Franck Nijhof’s guide to November’s “What the Heck?!” month gives households a concrete route for reporting frustrations. Search the dedicated community-forum category first, add experience and votes to an existing topic, or create one topic per problem. Describe what happened and what was expected; a technical solution is unnecessary.

The guide asks the person maintaining Home Assistant to help others at home post in their own words. The category is scheduled to stay open throughout November. Votes do not guarantee a fix, and requests for new integrations or apps belong on GitHub.

externalSources.title: “What the Heck?!” 2026: Everyone at home gets a say

articles.title: Matter.js keeps devices discoverable as network addresses change
articles.dek: Fresh addresses replace stale ones, while ending one advertisement stops hiding another.
body: Devices built with Matter.js refresh their network advertisements when the host’s addresses change, such as after an internet provider assigns a new IPv6 prefix. The library checks once a minute and announces the current addresses, instead of leaving controllers looking for addresses that no longer exist.

Related work keeps shared address records alive when a pairing advertisement ends or one connected smart-home network is removed. Previously, withdrawing that advertisement could also tell controllers to forget addresses still needed by the device’s other connections.
These corrections apply to software built with Matter.js. They do not resolve every network-interface change: receiving discovery requests on a completely new interface still needs separate work.

pullRequests.title: fix(protocol): follow interface address changes in mDNS and GeneralDiagnostics
fix(protocol): a goodbye names only records no remaining service publishes

articles.title: Music Assistant brings podcast transcripts to its phone app
articles.dek: Episode pages and the expanded player can display text supplied by the podcast source.
body: Music Assistant’s phone app adds a dedicated podcast-episode page with its description, played state, duration and a link back to the podcast. An Other episodes tab keeps the rest of the series within reach.

When the source supplies a transcript, the page and expanded player display it through the app’s lyrics view, including timing and offset controls. Transcript loading requires server interface version 81 or newer. This extends the episode and transcript experience covered on the web player in October to the phone app.

pullRequests.title: Add the podcast episode page with the transcript

articles.title: ESPHome stops servo blinds moving when their control signal ends
articles.dek: Finishing the last pulse avoids the unintended movement seen after automatic detachment.
body: ESPHome corrects a brief, unwanted servo movement when an ESP32 stops driving its control signal. Setting the output to zero previously cut the final pulse short; the correction lets that pulse finish before applying zero at the next cycle.
Tomas Matheson reproduced blinds sporadically reopening after automatic detachment and reports that the correction stops it on his setup. This is his first contribution to ESPHome.

pullRequests.title: [ledc] Fix pulse truncation when setting zero duty

articles.title: Music Assistant lets integrations speak through Yandex Stations
articles.dek: A separate opt-in command can send requests to Alice and reach the linked Yandex account.
body: Music Assistant’s Yandex Station connection adds commands that let integrations make a speaker say a phrase in Alice’s voice or pass Alice a text request as though it had been spoken. The request command starts disabled because it can reach everything connected to the Yandex account; the owner must enable it explicitly.

The connection also recognizes music Alice starts on the speaker. With a linked Yandex Music account, it shows the track and artwork and can add it to that account’s favourites. The contributor tested the commands and playback handling on a Yandex Station Mini 2.

pullRequests.title: Update Yandex Station provider to v1.7.9: Alice speech API commands and report-driven playback state

articles.title: Music Assistant identifies more differently named album tracks
articles.dek: Matching a complete album’s order and timings helps when streaming services use different titles.
body: Music Assistant identifies more streamed album tracks when services use different titles from the MusicBrainz catalogue. If an entire album’s track order and timings line up, each track can receive the matching recording identity without a title match.

Local files retain the title check, as do albums whose track count, numbering or durations do not line up. In the contributor’s test of twelve albums containing 637 tracks, identified tracks increased from 310 to 603; one St Matthew Passion recording went from none to all seventy tracks.

pullRequests.title: Match an album's tracks to MusicBrainz in order when the whole album lines up

articles.title: Home Assistant adjusts computer displays through System Bridge
articles.dek: Compatible screens gain brightness and power controls, with separate readings for each connected display.
body: Home Assistant adds brightness and power controls for computer displays through System Bridge. Each screen that reports the relevant capability gets a brightness control from 0 to 100 percent, a power switch, or both.

Disconnected screens become unavailable. A monitor that cannot carry out a command reports System Bridge’s error instead of pretending it succeeded. The contributor checked brightness control on a Linux laptop’s built-in panel; support still depends on the display and its control interface.

pullRequests.title: Add System Bridge display brightness and power controls
Document System Bridge display brightness and power controls

articles.title: Home Assistant guides La Marzocco owners through required policy acceptance
articles.dek: Setup and sign-in recovery show the manufacturer’s privacy-policy step when cloud access is blocked.
body: Home Assistant adds a privacy-policy acceptance step for La Marzocco owners whose cloud connection is blocked until they accept the manufacturer’s latest terms. It appears during initial setup or when an existing connection needs to sign in again.

The step accepts the required privacy policy and offers separate optional profiling and commercial consents. Afterward, setup continues to the machine selection or sign-in recovery that was interrupted.

pullRequests.title: Ask to accept the La Marzocco privacy policy in config and reauth flows

articles.title: Home Assistant repairs AI connections through Cloud addresses
articles.dek: A failed icon lookup no longer prevents the Model Context Protocol connection from starting.
body: Home Assistant repairs Model Context Protocol connections made through Home Assistant Cloud or another address outside its configured URL list. The server could fail during the initial connection while trying to construct its icon address, before the connected AI application could use its tools.
The connection uses the address of the incoming request for its icon. Related handling recognizes Home Assistant Cloud custom domains too.

pullRequests.title: Use the request origin for MCP server icon URLs
Prefer cloud custom domains in get_url

articles.title: Home Assistant shows when Homematic refuses to arm
articles.dek: A dedicated status lets dashboards and automations respond to a rejected alarm command.
body: Home Assistant adds an Arming blocked status for Homematic IP Cloud alarm systems. It turns on when an arm command from Home Assistant is refused, such as because a window is open or a device is unreachable.

The status clears after the next command succeeds. It records the outcome of an attempted command rather than continuously predicting whether arming will work, and it does not add an override to arm anyway.

pullRequests.title: Add an arming blocked sensor to HomematicIP Cloud
